item: The keyword rollup build fits DuckDB's 1,004 MB tier: stage cut by keyword_id into limit-derived shards, each aggregated and dropped in turn, a shard that runs out of memory halved and then declined as duckdb-limit
summary: The single GROUP BY over one in-memory stage needed about 2,000 MiB for 12 M mentions, so on the 1,004 MB tier (encrypted corpus, no spill) the build stopped every boot. Now sharded by keyword_id with the count derived from the limit (peak = base + aggregate/k + overhead*k, fitted to six measured peaks, reproduced by a test within 5%); peak 602 MiB DuckDB / 896 MB RSS on a seeded 12 M-mention corpus, digests identical to the single pass, build time 1% to 4% slower. A failed shard leaves the previous rollup untouched; out-of-memory halves the shard up to 16 parts, then declines as duckdb-limit with shards/shard/split in the kept stop; BUILD_CODE_VERSION 2 releases single-pass stops. Inferred, not streamed: figures above 12 M mentions. Constants measured on DuckDB 1.5.6.
